text_blocks.snippet: A tax deed is a legal document that conveys ownership of a property to a buyer when the property is sold at a tax sale due to unpaid property taxes. Essentially, it's the instrument used to transfer title after a property is auctioned off because the owner failed to pay their taxes.
snippet_highlighted_words: a legal document that conveys ownership of a property to a buyer when the property is sold at a tax sale due to unpaid property taxes

list.title: Tax Sales:
list.snippet: When property taxes go unpaid, the local government can initiate a tax sale (often an auction) to recover the delinquent taxes.

list.title: Tax Deed as the Conveyance:
list.snippet: The tax deed is the document that officially transfers ownership of the property from the delinquent taxpayer to the winning bidder at the tax sale.

list.title: Redemption Period:
list.snippet: In many jurisdictions, there's a redemption period after the tax sale, during which the original owner can still reclaim their property by paying the outstanding taxes plus interest and penalties, according to iBuyer.com.

list.title: Tax Deed vs. Tax Lien:
list.snippet: In some states, instead of selling tax deeds, the government sells tax liens, which give the investor the right to collect the unpaid taxes and potentially foreclose if they are not paid. California is one example of a state that uses tax deeds instead of tax liens at www.digonzini.com.

list.title: Recording the Tax Deed:
list.snippet: The tax deed needs to be recorded with the county (or relevant local government) to make the transfer of ownership official. In some jurisdictions, there are deadlines for recording the tax deed.

related_questions.snippet: The average tax rate is the total amount of tax divided by total income. For example, if a household has a total income of $100,000 and pays taxes of $15,000, the household's average tax rate is 15 percent. The marginal tax rate is the incremental tax paid as a percentage of additional income.
